title: agent-atlas Orchestrator manifest
description: The single control plane. It owns the deterministic control flow — deciding which task/agent runs, in what order, and on what condition — and externalizes run state. There is one orchestrator per model; the tasks are its children.

control_flow.description: How the orchestrator expresses control flow: a state machine, a DAG, or a simple sequence.

state_store.description: id of a System (kind=state-store) where run/step state is externalized.

compliance_regimes.description: Model-level: the compliance standards this whole system claims to satisfy (NIST AI RMF vocabulary). System-governing regimes like SOC 2 / FedRAMP / EU AI Act live HERE (they govern the system, not a single field); per-object data classes (PHI/PII/PCI) live in each object's governance.data_tags. MULTIPLE apply.

governance.description: Regime-neutral trust/privacy controls (NIST AI RMF: privacy, security, accountability). Optional — declare what the requirements state; leave the rest for a human.

data_classification.description: Sensitivity of the data this object touches.

data_tags.description: Regulatory data classes (MULTIPLE may apply, e.g. PHI and PII).

residency.description: Where data may be processed/stored. 'on-prem' = never leaves the boundary.

redaction.description: Fields to filter/redact/drop before telemetry is indexed.
